articles.headline: Halifax Parents Hoping To Reverse Nine-Year-Old’s $20,000 Roblox Bill
keyFacts: A Halifax couple discovered their nine-year-old son spent $28,000 on in-game purchases through a shared Apple Pay account.
Most gaming companies refunded the charges, but Roblox has not refunded the $20,000 spent on its game.
Roblox stated the purchases were made via a third party and directed the family to contact the merchant for review.
body: Ever since video games entered the family home, so began the eternal schism between confused parents and the most popular software. PokÃ©mon. Grand Theft Auto. Which one is Zelda anyway. It never ends. But only in recent history has this generational divide begun to carry an unsuspecting price tag. A Halifax couple were stunned to discover that their nine-year-old son racked up tens of thousands in fees while gaming. Though successful in reversing the charges from most parties, Roblox remains a holdout, where the kid managed to spend $20 grand.
“He enters buttons and ta-da,” says mother Dawn Sutherland (no relation to the other, Canadian Don Sutherland). “He has no clue that he has spent any money.”

According to CTV News, Nova Scotians Carey Chernoff and Dawn Sutherland were unaware of the massive tab their son had accrued over a summer of gaming. Each member of the household has their own iPad, but each is linked to a shared Apple Pay account. After receiving an alert that their Mastercard was maxed out, the parents discovered their son had spent $28,000 (roughly $19,000 USD) through in-game purchases. They say that upon asking to be refunded, most of the gaming companies complied, with the exception of one. With the lionâs share of the bill, the two are hoping Roblox will be more reasonable.

In a statement to CTV, Roblox said that “These purchases were made via a third party. We encourage the family to reach out to the merchant for review of the transactions.” The implied third party could be Apple, who did not respond to CTV’s request for comment.
“It so easily can happen to anyone,” says Sutherland. “It terrifies most parents.”

Itâs an increasingly common story. In fact, itâs not even the only Roblox spending scandal on CTV in recent history. The sum does leave a bigger dent than most others, however. And while Roblox does offer parental controls, including those around spending limits, itâs clear that these features arenât incredibly well communicated among the public.

Though older than most of its user base, Roblox is immensely popular among young children. The responsibility that comes with maintaining an adolescent demographic has rarely been met by the company, and their responses to criticism leaves much to be desired. While parents should better monitor their childrenâs media and gaming habits, thereâs also plenty of room for better policy on in-game spending. Around the globe, consumer protection bureaus have begun to target long-running monetization practices, though these policy trends are typically slower-moving in North America.

articles.headline: Cowboys’ Brandon Aubrey reveals how new partnership boosts his confidence on and off the field
keyFacts: Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey partnered with Invisalign to improve his smile and boost his confidence.
Aubrey pursued an NFL kicking career after his wife encouraged him to transition from software engineering.
Aubrey said Invisalign clear aligners fit his busy schedule because they are removable and doctors provide necessary care resources.
body: Brandon Aubrey's path to becoming an NFL kicker parallels his new Invisalign campaign.

Before the Dallas Cowboys kicker took the field, he played soccer and then worked as a software engineer. In an exclusive interview with The Sporting News, he explained that his mindset put him on his trajectory to the NFL, which began with staying confident, something that his parents invested in at a young age.

"My parents put a lot of time and money into it, and I didn't take care of it well enough, and it shifted," he said of his previous Invisalign aligners. "I'm trying to find a way to invest in my overall well-being, my smile, my confidence, and I think Invisalign, clear aligners, just fit that perfectly for me. So I'm just really excited to work with Invisalign and get going and get my smile back to the way I want it."
Aubrey credits his wife, Jenn Aubrey, for giving him the idea to pursue becoming an NFL kicker after seeing how being a software engineer wasn't fulfilling for him.

"My wife could tell that I just wasn't quite happy doing it, and she kind of pushed me and said, 'Hey,' as we're watching a football game, 'I think you could do that.' And that was the moment that gave me the idea to do it," he recalled.
He quickly learned that his soccer skills came in handy for his future career pivot.

"We just went out to a field and kicked a few balls around," he continued. "And that day, I was able to make one from 60 without any real training. So that's when I thought, this is a crazy idea, a long shot, but I've got nothing to lose."

Given that Brandon wasn't ready to retire as a soccer player, he had to shift his mindset again so that he was prepared to hit the NFL field once he discovered how transferable his soccer skills were to football.

"I'd say it comes from being able to look back at my career as a soccer player and kind of identify the things I didn't do well that made me have to retire before I was ready to retire," the Dallas kicker shared. "And that's just, I was scared on the field of making mistakes. And that's a mindset that you cannot have as a professional athlete. You'll be half a second slower than your opponents when thinking about what you can't do. You won't take necessary risks that you need to stand out. I wouldn't go out for a 65-yard field goal if I was scared of making mistakes."

He then began relaying this mantra back to himself to break out of quickly resetting after an error so that he could continue making his goals, "So that's something I committed to myself when I started kicking: you've already made this mistake once. We're not going to do it again. You've got nothing to lose. You've already embarrassed yourself once, so just go out there and kick the ball."
How Brandon Aubrey's Partnership with Invisalign Works With His Demanding NFL Schedule

Over 18 weeks, Brandon, who is a vital part of the Cowboys roster, has to make sure that any additions to his personal life can fit into his schedule. From travel games, practice, and everything in between, it doesn't leave much room in his busy schedule. Luckily, Invisalign makes the cut.

"So Invisalign clear aligners are just a great option for me," the three-time Pro Bowler explained. "They're removable, pretty much invisible, which makes them just a great option for me and the doctors I'm working with are doing a great job of kind of sending me home with resources I need to take care of it as I go through a busy day."

articles.headline: Wyoming keeper comes up big again as Cowboys win state title
keyFacts: Wyoming defeated Worthington Christian 3-1 in a penalty-kick shootout to win the Division IV boys soccer state championship.
Goalkeeper Teddy Peterson saved two penalty kicks to help Wyoming earn its second state title.
The teams were tied 1-1 through regulation and overtime before Wyoming made all three of its shootout attempts.
body: COLUMBUS, Ohio – For the second time this week, Wyoming junior Teddy Peterson came up big in goal in a penalty-kick shootout with all to play for.

Wyoming went to penalty kicks in its quest for a state boys soccer title, defeating Worthington Christian to win the Ohio High School Athletic Association Division IV boys soccer state championship Nov. 15 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Stadium.

Wyoming, 17-4-3 overall, won 3-1 in a best-of-five penalty-kick shootout to win its second state title, its first in 2021. WC (18-3-3), last year's state champion in DIV, finished as runner-up for the third time in the past four seasons. It is the 19th boys soccer state final all-time to be decided in a shootout.
Peterson, Wyoming's first-year starter in goal, saved two penalty kicks in the shootout, including the last Warriors kick in the fourth round to end it.
After both teams made their first kick, Peterson saved WC's second, and the Warriors' third shooter missed well over the crossbar.
Wyoming was a perfect 3-for-3 in the shootout, with seniors Miles Steininger, Nolan Franco and Brayden Strong converting in order.
Peterson had made the final save in the semifinals, ending the game after Liam Hagerman had converted to start the seventh round.
How the game unfolded
The game was evenly played through 80 minutes of regulation and 30 minutes of overtime.
Wyoming had 16 shots, four on goal. Worthington had 14, five on goal. Three of those came in one wild sequence late in the first half.
Both teams showed the strong defense they have had all season. Worthington allowed only 20 goals for the season and Wyoming 17. Both teams scored in the second half today.
Wyoming took a 1-0 lead six minutes into the second half.
Junior Liam Hagerman hit a right-footed grounder just inside the near post for his seventh goal of the season.
Hagerman had scored twice in the postseason in blowout wins in the first two rounds. His four goals in the regular season were in similar situations.
Those goals prepared him for the much-needed clutch moments this week. He had the winning penalty kick in the seventh round against Bay Village Bay in the state semifinals.
Hagerman had two more shots on goal in the last 15 minutes left in the second half, after Worthington tied it at 1-1. He had all three shots on goal for the Cowboys in regulation.
With 21 minutes left, WC's Colton Hoskinson volleyed in the ball near the far post from a great diagonal pass to tie the game 1-1.
Both teams had multiple chances in overtime but shots missed wide. Nolan Franco had Wyoming's best chance in the second overtime.

With 13 minutes left in the first half, Worthington had a sequence where the Warriors had a header blocked by an outfield player, a follow shot clip the bottom of the crossbar, then a follow header saved by the keeper Peterson.
WC had seven shots in the first half, two on goal, both of those credited in that sequence. Wyoming had three shots, none on goal.
For regulation, Wyoming had eight shots, three on goal and WC had 12, five on goal.

Worthington came in as the defending state champions and was runner-up the previous two seasons. The Warriors had four state champions overall coming in and five runner-ups, plus six previous trips to the semifinals.
Wyoming was state champion in 2021, starting a run of four state semifinal appearances in six seasons.
Wyoming lineup notes and statistics
Wyoming starters in the final were Peterson, Will Haid, Ethan Nordstrom, Brayden Strong, Nolan Franco, Caleb Kahn, Miles Steininger, Everett Johnson, Carter Snyder, Dawson Feldman and Cayden Walters.

Five of them scored in double figures for the year and were closely match. Snyder had 13 goals and five assists. Johnson had 12 and 11, Franco 11 and nine, Steininger 10 and 12 and Walters 10 and five. Hagerman and junior Ethan Harrison had seven goals and Kahn five. Dennis Cummings had eight assists and three goals.
Peterson finished with 11.5 shutouts in goal.
Wyoming senior salute

Seniors are Will Haid, Ethan Nordstrom, AJ Nikolaidis, Brayden Strong, Nolan Franco, Caleb Kahn, Tristan Pitman, Miles Steininger, Everett Johnson, Carter Snyder, Greg Kleinschmidt and Dennis Cummings.

articles.headline: Why Raiders fans are planning to stay seated for Fernando Mendoza's first TD
keyFacts: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start in Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks.
Raiders fans plan to remain seated during Mendoza's first touchdown as a tribute to his mother, who uses a wheelchair.
Mendoza is the first No. 1 overall pick quarterback to make his first start against the defending Super Bowl champions.
body: With Kirk Cousins traded back to the Minnesota Vikings, Las Vegas Raiders fans' wait to see 2026 first-round pick Fernando Mendoza start is over. However, they may wait to jump for joy upon Mendoza scoring a touchdown at home against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 until he scores his second touchdown.

The reason behind this is a wholesome one. Mendoza's mother, Elsa, utilizes a wheelchair while dealing with multiple sclerosis (MS), so fans are trying to organize a tribute to her, Mendoza, and his family by remaining seated if/when he scores against Seattle on Sunday. For those who watched Mendoza's college career, TV cameras often cut to his family celebrating, and Mendoza's father, Fernando Sr., would often be seen seated and hugging Elsa after touchdowns. Fernando Sr. also remained seated as he and Elsa's son was drafted first overall in the 2026 NFL draft.

"I see her fighting every single day, and with a smile on her face," Mendoza said of his mother during a pre-draft appearance on The Rich Eisen Show. "So there's no excuse for me to have a bad day, bad play or bad game. I'm always trying to have an optimistic approach, give the best and serve the best to my teammates."
Obviously, there will still be Raiders fans who get so excited they leave their seats when Mendoza scores his first NFL touchdown, but it's a thoughtful gesture.
Listen, everyone going to Allegiant Stadium this Sunday. Stay seated when Fernando scores his first touchdown. Will be an epic gesture from fans to player. Pass it along.
— Tom Joanides (@TJoanides) November 11, 2026

It's unclear when Mendoza's first touchdown may happen, though. He will be the first No. 1 overall quarterback in NFL history to make his first career start versus the defending Super Bowl champions. Seattle also enters Week 10 leading the entire league in total defense (244.2 total yards per game allowed), which means Mendoza will also be the first No. 1 overall pick quarterback to make his first career start against the NFL's No. 1 total defense since Vinny Testaverde in 1987. However, new Raiders coach Klint Kubiak was the Seahawks offensive coordinator last season, so perhaps he has told Mendoza some vulnerabilities the Seahawks defense has that other teams may not be as aware of.
Either way, many Raiders fans will be glued to their seats at Allegiant Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

articles.headline: Spain v England: Nations League – live
keyFacts: England scored three goals against Spain in a Nations League match through Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White.
England player Elliot Anderson received a red card and conceded a penalty to Spain in the 64th minute.
Harry Kane's first-half goal marked his seventh consecutive away match with a goal for England.
body: 67 min Someone on the England bench is booked, and I wonder if Tuchel contemplates a change. He needs keep an out-ball, but perhaps midfield control means he remove Rogers for, perhaps, Lewis-Skelly.
PENALTY TO SPAIN AND A RED CARD FOR ELLIOT ANDERSON!

64 min That question, eh? How will England eff it up? Like thus: Quansah is mugged by Lamine, the first time England have been so caught, and when Baena sweeps him in, Anderson hauls him back, a rash call, and Spain have a route back into the game!
62 min “Are you Scotland in disguise?” sing the away end, a disbelieving Philip Cornwall back in touch BUT EXCUSE ME WHILE I INTERRUPT MYSELF ONCE MORE!
61 min Gordon, who’s having a fine night, win another corner, and England will fancy another here, but this time Rice’s floaty delivery is easily fielded by Simon.

60 min And what a moment of redemption that is for White. Jeered by his own fans after leaving the World Cp squad in 2022, he’s nicely reintegrated now, and that was the kind of finish you’d expect to see from Pedro Porro. That is some serious praise.

Kane across the face of the box to Bellingham, who caresses in behind for White! He takes a touch, narrowing the angle but forcing the keeper to move then, when Simon spreads himself, he picks a very deliberate finish through the keeper’s legs! This is a hiding!

56 min Bellingham, whose good work won the corner from which England scored, wins another ion similar style, this time down the left, as we see footgge of the England goal, Tuchel on the touchline also applying brow to imaginary ball – that’s how much time and space Konsa had. This time, the corner comes to nowt.
54 min Minor Spain protests for a free-kick of some sort, but VAR isn’t interested. Konsa couldn’t have been freer, the question on everybody’s lips a familiar one: how will they eff it up from here?
A Rice outswinger and, in the middle of the box, Konsa has maybe five yards of space all around him to run in and guide home from seven yards. England are all over this!

52 min Zubimendi picks up a poor pass and punches between Anderosn and Rice, finding Lamine … whose trivela cross is straight at Trafford. Then England find Bellingham down the right of the box and he delays well before winning a corner off Pedri, gesticulating to where he thinks the away end is, but isn’t.

49 min Lamine spreads wide to Cucurella, then Spain work it back to him, Hall delaying before Gordon confiscates possession. Those two have been brilliant so far and, when England counter, Rogers cuts inside Cucurella, who trips him and is booked.

48 min England win it high and win a throw, Tuchel’s alacrity in returning the ball evidencing their intent to speed up the game and impose their will. Spain soon have possession back, but it’s a message not to retreat.
Elsewhere, France are level at 0-0 playing Turkey in Bordeaux; Belgium have come from 1-0 down to lead Italy 3-1. As it stands, it’ll be France and Belgium moving on, Italy’s renaissance curtailed.
“Benitez, Robbie Fowler’s last game for Liverpool,” writes Paul Oakes. “Takes him off with five minutes to go. Liverpool get a penalty one minute later.”
I guess the idea was right, though – a proper reception.

“What did Ferguson do against Chelsea in 2010?” asks Joshua Keeling. In a game United needed to not lose, he picked Nevlle, Giggs and Scholes, though younger, harder-running players had excelled against Bayern the previous midweek, United lost the game, lost the title, and lost the chance of four in a row.

I wonder if De la Fuente will move to Pedri; the control we expect from Spain isn’t there tonight, and his ability to tempo-set might change this game. So far, Merino has been a cone, and it’s no great surprise; he’s a late-doors player, one who finds a goal when you’re desperate for one, rather than someone who gets involved in general play.

Argy-bargy between White and Ruiz as the players depart; Spain aren’t usually worried like this, the plan Tuchel had for the bigger games at the World Cup finally executed. The second period should be a belter.

45+2 min “England fans here singing ‘The best in the world, the best in the woorrrrld, Harry Kane, the best in the world’,” messages Philip Cornwall, our production editor and man in the stands. There aren’t many places he’s not been watching England; I wonder where this half ranks in terms of quality against quality. In my lifetime, it’s high up there.
Kane takes a deep breath, then punches into the far corner, a third of the way up. England have earned that, and Kane has now scored in seven straight away games.

43 min Spain want a free-kick for a foul on Cucurella, but I don’t see it – he went in as hard as Bellingham, then Anderson caught him in follow-through after making a pass; Clement Turpin, the ref, is having none of it. Here we go, and this is pressure, considering what happened at Wembley. The whistling is serious…

41 min Cucurella and Bellingham contest a 50-50, the ball landing perfectly for Anderson, who controls a terrific long, low pass, curving around the outside of the Spain block for Kane. He knows he’s not got the pace to do Cubarsi on the outside, so he holds then explodes on the inside and Cubarsi’s challenge is lazy, taking man and nothing else.

40 min Baena picks up the ball just outside the box and picks a lovely pass, punched straight and in behind for Lamine … but Hall, who’s enjoying himself, stretches to intercept. England have defended really well so far.
39 min Hall crosses from the left and Belling ham is up on the far side, but can’t wrap his head around enough of the ball to knock it back across and Simon gathers.

38 min “Lenny Walker’s decision to bring on Dale Banton for Aldershot (as was then) late on against Halfax at The Rec in, ooh, 1990(?) was pretty dreadful,” reckons David Johnson. “Fluffed a load of chances. Cost The Shots a ... hmm ... shot at eighth place and a potential run for the Fourth Division playoffs that year. Surely up there.”

36 min Again, England jump on Zubimendi, Gordon at him and finding Rogers, who flips a square pass towards the back post, but Laporte does enough to flick away. Immediately Spain counter with Lamine down the right; he snaps a curler that flies just wide, though had it been on target, I think Pickford would’ve got it.
35 min “1970 World Cup quarter final, England v West Germany,” says Rhys Davies. “Ramsey took off Bobby Charlton, freeing up Beckenbauer. The rest is history.”
Yup, that might be the daddy – Norman Hunter for Martin Peters was also a vibe.

31 min Kane drops deep and accepts the ball on the back foot, under pressure … and Ruiz robs him, but England quickly win it back. They look really well organised in terms of defensive structure but, more than that, there’s a desire from each individual to take responsibility. The question, though, is whether they can keep that focus and discipline across 90 minutes, and whether their attackers can create; it’s been a while since they exerted serious pressure on the Spain defence.
30 min It’s a bit messy now, which England won’t mind. They’re set up for a physical contest, and the more play is broken, the more they’re able to enforce that advantage.

28 min Tuchel’s performance against Argentina is surely one of the great managerial eff-ups; which others spring to mind? Those in my head: Pep Guardiola, Man City v Chelsea in the 2021 Champions League final; Alex Ferguson, Man United v Chelsea 2010. Any more for any more?

26 min Cucurella and Baena combine down the left and Ruiz’s subsequent cross is a goodun, but Quansah does really well to head clear, the ball landing on Porro’s laces … and ensuing volley landing I don’t even know where.

25 min Simon takes a liberty, drilling a hopeful pass through the middle of the pitch to which Konsa is first. He meets the ball with a solid header, finding Bellingham, who I think is offside, and once the shot slides by the near post, the flag is raised.

23 min We’re into that 4-4-2-block stage, Spain pinning them back into their shape, and Lamine slipping a pass into Baena, through the legs of Barcelona teammate Gordon; I doubt this is the last he’ll hear of a shameful episode.

21 min Yup, Pedro Porro replaces Pubill – a change I think may actually help Spain, the new man’s first-phase excellence, ability to invert and goal-threat of greater use than the physicality they’re losing.

18 min And here comes Hall, picking a diag that takes him from touchline to box, beating two men with Rogers bumrushing the near post. The cross, though, is blocked behind then, when the corner comes in, another inswinging brute from Rice, Kane heads past the far post. He’ll be relieved the flag goes up, for that was a chance.

17 min The game has settled after that rabid England start, Spain much more of a factor now, but here come England again, Anderson megging Merino and Kane moving the ball on. Nothing comes of it, but England step on to them again!
14 min Already, the inclusion of Merino is giving Spain a problem – when he drops, Quansah is following him, and he’s not able to make the extra man in midfield.

11 min England’s press is excellent, its latest application forcing Simon to kick long; Wimblespain! Of course, at some point, the pass-and-move is likely to assume control, but if Tuchel’s men can grab a goal, they’ve the ability on the counter to add to it.

9 min This is the best nine minutes England have played under Tuchel and probably Southgate too, bristling with confidence, intensity and menace. Gordon gets Pubill squared, barges by on the outside … but his cut-back is into traffic.

articles.headline: Goodbye, overtourism? Community-based travel gaining ground
keyFacts: Latin America is experiencing a tourism boom that causes overtourism challenges at sites like Machu Picchu, UN Tourism and officials reported.
Experts and survey data indicate that travelers increasingly prefer community-based tourism and smaller group sizes over traditional travel models.
Tourism specialists stated that sustainable growth requires giving local communities direct control over development and access to financing.
body: Latin America is currently one of the world's most dynamic tourism regions. According to UN Tourism, the United Nations agency responsible for promoting responsible tourism, international arrivals in South America grew by 7% last year, while Central America saw a 5% increase, both above the global average.

But the boom comes at a price: overtourism. In some destinations, the sheer number of visitors is creating environmental and social problems, fueling tensions and raising questions about who really benefits from the business.

One famous example is Machu Picchu, the Inca citadel in Peru, which lures up to 5,600 visitors a day. In 2025, Peru's official watchdog warned that more tickets were being sold than permitted, potentially putting the site at risk of being added to UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger. The UNESCO World Heritage Committee has already expressed its concern.

In a bid to protect the Galapagos Islands and its bountiful ecosystems that inspired Charles Darwin, Ecuador doubled the entrance fee for foreign visitors to $200 in 2024. Even so, pressure is mounting to construct new hotels and tourist apartments. And in Mexico City, the influx of tourists and digital nomads into neighborhoods such as Roma and Condesa has fueled protests over rising rents.

What can be done to make tourism more inclusive and sustainable? That's one of the industry's biggest questions. At ITB Americas, an international travel trade fair in Guadalajara, Mexico, DW spoke with three experts.
Sustainable travel moving from niche to mainstream

Richard Bazan is a regional manager for the Americas at Planeterra, a nonprofit organization that promotes and supports community-based tourism. He said several trends are emerging: group sizes are shrinking and travelers are seeking more intimate experiences.
"Where groups of 20 used to travel together, now it's four or five," he told DW.

So-called "nature-positive" tourism is also gaining traction, with travel programs that help fund, for example, reforestation projects. Bazan said even all-inclusive resorts are realizing that they can no longer shut themselves off from their surroundings. Instead, they need to offer authentic experiences that connect visitors with the destination.
"Community-based tourism is no longer a niche," he said.

Pressure for change is also coming from travelers themselves. According to Booking.com's 2025 annual survey, which polled 32,000 people in 34 countries, 93% said they wanted to make more sustainable travel choices. For the first time, more than half (53%) were aware of tourism's impact on local communities, not just the environment.
Communities know what's best for their land

Sarah Payne, director of the Reset Tourism Fund at the UnTours Foundation, pointed to the underlying problem. In the traditional tourism business model, most of the money generated never reaches local communities, the people who actually live with the influx of visitors.

"Access to financing is key, yet extremely difficult for communities," she explained. The financial products on the market tend to be expensive and inflexible, as tourism is considered a high-risk sector. Her foundation's fund offers low-interest loans with flexible repayment terms. Its guiding principle is that communities generally know what's best for their own land.

Sebastian Munoz, co-founder of Rutopia, a platform specializing in ecotourism and community-based tourism, has brought his experience from the nonprofit sector into social enterprise. His believes tours must be designed in partnership with communities so they feel a sense of ownership, rather than seeing them as something imposed from outside.

Bazan, meanwhile, thinks community-based tourism should not be approached as a humanitarian project, but through a market-driven lens: understanding what visitors are looking for and then planning hand-in-hand with the local community. In other words, building bridges between these two distinct worlds.
"It's not sustainable to create a product if no one comes to experience it," he said.
The challenge: Rethinking growth

The big question is how to grow without sacrificing sustainability. For Bazan, that decision doesn't belong to the tourism industry. Communities themselves must decide how they want to grow, and outside players should not pressure them. Their role, he said, is to amplify local voices, not to bring solutions or investments. "We have to learn to listen," he said.

The impact of community-based tourism is difficult to measure, Munoz acknowledged, because it has social impacts that go beyond the numbers. He cited the example of the Indigenous Mixtec community in Mexico that receives tourists interested in learning the local language. Suddenly, children who today speak only Spanish began joining the classes and asking their grandparents to teach them the language, too.

For Munoz, community-based tourism can be a powerful tool for valuing cultural and regional diversity. It's about creating value over the long term — and that, he said, is where the real experience for visitors lies.
The experts agree that change is slow. But they argue it's worth the effort: If there is more respect for local people and environments, in the end, everyone goes home happier.
This article was originally written in Spanish.

articles.headline: FAA ground stop timeline: Weekend chaos grounds planes and postpones games
keyFacts: The FAA grounded flights nationwide for over four hours Friday after a communications failure disrupted radar feeds, officials said.
The outage caused thousands of flight cancellations and delays, stranding travelers and forcing several sports teams to postpone games.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said air travel will likely return fully to normal by Monday as investigators test the equipment.
body: A communications failure brought departures across the country to a halt Friday, stranding travelers, disrupting professional sports teams and sending federal officials scrambling to restore flights and determine what went wrong.

The longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years ended after more than four hours, but the fallout stretched through the weekend as airlines worked through cancellations and investigators zeroed in on routers tied to the outage.
Here’s a timeline of the shutdown and the federal response. All times are Eastern.
4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said officials detected instability in radar data and communications at 3:36 p.m., affecting facilities that guide planes approaching airports and traveling between them.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) halted departures nationwide at 3:54 p.m. as controllers and pilots followed procedures to bring aircraft already airborne safely to the ground. About 3,500 flights were in the air.
FAA SAYS AIR TRAVEL SHOULD BE BACK TO NORMAL SUNDAY AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP
Duffy later emphasized that officials had not lost every radar feed or all telecommunications service. The inconsistent information was enough to trigger the shutdown as a safety precaution.
Duffy said the ground stop was necessary because of "a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."
FAA technicians were investigating, he said.
The disruption also prompted a broader federal response as officials examined whether the failure could have involved malicious activity.
BUTTIGIEG TAKES SWIPE AT TRUMP ADMINISTRATION AMID FAA FLIGHT CHAOS

President Donald Trump brought federal agencies together on a call Friday, including intelligence officials, the FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Intelligence partners reported they were not detecting the usual signs of a cyberattack, Duffy said.

Steven Cheung, assistant to the president and White House director of communications, later said on X that the White House and administration had acted within minutes of the FAA notice, crediting Trump for the response.
UPDATED START TIMES FOR COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAMES AFFECTED BY FAA GROUND STOP, BROKEN DOWN BY CONFERENCE
"Minutes after the FAA notice posted, the White House and Administration sprang into action. Because of that speed and effectiveness, the ground stop was lifted after just a few hours," Cheung wrote.
"A Herculean effort, only made possible by President Trump's leadership."
NFL OFFICIAL DON WILLARD WILL REFEREE TWO GAMES IN ONE DAY AFTER FAA GROUND STOP DISRUPTS TRAVEL, LEAGUE SAYS

Speaking to reporters outside the White House on Friday, Nov. 13, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a nefarious attack and reassured Americans with loved ones traveling.
"There’s no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," Mullin said.
TENNESSEE VOLUNTEERS OVERCOME SLUGGISH OFFENSE, JET LAG TO TAKE DOWN TEXAS A&M AND KEEP CFP HOPES ALIVE

The shutdown also left college football teams scrambling to reach Saturday’s games. Texas had already boarded its plane for Baton Rouge to face LSU when the ground stop prevented departure. Tennessee’s scheduled 4 p.m. flight to College Station was also halted.
Teams including Ole Miss, Tennessee and Baylor returned to their athletic facilities as officials weighed alternate travel plans. Some teams sat aboard charter planes for up to two hours.
PRIVATE PLANES AND ROADTRIPS: AEW GOES ABOVE AND BEYOND TO GET TO PHOENIX FOR FULL GEAR DESPITE TRAVEL CHAOS
The shutdown also disrupted travel for professional sports teams ahead of a busy weekend.

The Brooklyn Nets were trying to fly from New Orleans to Memphis when their flight was halted, according to The Associated Press. The Memphis Grizzlies were also in New Orleans for a Friday game against the Pelicans, with plans to depart afterward.

The Cleveland Cavaliers and Chicago Bulls also had planned postgame flights. The San Jose Sharks’ flight to Utah for a Saturday game against the Mammoth did not depart before the shutdown, while the Detroit Pistons had reached Miami earlier Friday.
The FAA lifted the nationwide order at 8:15 p.m., allowing departures to resume.

Planes began leaving airports including LaGuardia, Los Angeles International and Reagan National . Some travelers at Reagan National had been waiting since around 3:30 p.m. for flights scheduled to leave around 4 p.m.
Duffy warned that reopening the airspace would not immediately get every flight moving. Departures depended on whether airlines had pilots, flight attendants and other crews available.
"It’s going to be slow," he said.

Lifting the ground stop did not immediately solve the travel problems for college teams. By 9:12 p.m. Friday, Washington, Texas, Tennessee and Oregon State were heading back to airports, but other programs faced crew availability problems.
Utah’s charter crew ran out of available hours, forcing the team to plan a Saturday morning departure for its game at Arizona. The Big 12 moved kickoff to 10:30 p.m. ET Saturday.
Just after midnight Saturday, the Ole Miss-Oklahoma game was moved to 1 p.m. ET Sunday after the Rebels were unable to leave Friday evening.
Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny said the school objected to the change but was told it would face a forfeit if it refused to play Sunday.
At a Saturday briefing, Duffy said contractor L3Harris had been replacing aging copper communications lines with fiber-optic connections at a remote FAA location.
The copper line was being discontinued, making the replacement necessary, he said.
During the work, a router began generating more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, overwhelming other routers and disrupting communications and radar feeds.
Investigators were examining whether installation error or faulty equipment caused the failure.
"Our contractor didn’t meet the moment or the equipment didn’t meet the moment," Duffy said.

Bedford distinguished the routine maintenance from the administration’s broader air traffic control modernization program. Duffy also said officials would reevaluate when such work should be performed.
FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said "the worst is behind us," with air travel expected to return to normal by the end of Sunday.
The Transportation Department said more than 8,000 flight operations resumed Friday night after the ground stop ended, but passengers continued facing delays and cancellations Saturday.
Airlines still needed to reposition aircraft and crews, leaving travelers scrambling to rebook and check whether their flights would operate.
Officials urged passengers to check directly with their airlines for current flight information.

Duffy said Sunday morning that air travel would improve throughout the day but probably would not return fully to normal until Monday, updating officials’ earlier prediction of a recovery by Sunday night.
Two routers from Texas and Arkansas were undergoing testing as investigators worked to determine the cause.

Duffy said work in El Dorado, Arkansas, was followed by problems involving equipment in Amarillo, Texas, where a system had been replaced about three weeks earlier. Engineers were examining the routers at an L3Harris laboratory in Florida.
"We think it was the installation or the router that was the bad actor," Duffy said.
He said there was no indication of a foreign cyberattack, while leaving open further investigation if new evidence emerged.

Duffy also pressed Congress for additional funding. He said the $12.5 billion already allocated covered specific upgrades, including radar, radios and electronic flight strips, but did not fund a replacement telecommunications network.
By 2 p.m. ET Sunday, 5,280 flights had been delayed and 1,709 canceled within, into or out of the U.S., according to FlightAware.
Dallas Fort Worth, Atlanta and Chicago O’Hare were among the hardest-hit airports tracked in the update, with hundreds of delays at each.
The disruptions continued Sunday afternoon as airlines worked to restore normal schedules.
FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP

United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby praised the FAA’s decision to halt flights and thanked employees and customers for their patience during the disruption. He also called for better technology and full staffing to help prevent future outages.
Kirby said he had spoken directly with Duffy, Bedford and aviation leaders from both parties in Congress about the impact on United’s passengers and employees.
"This moment must be a call to action," Kirby said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.
"It is critical for safety, our passengers, and our economy that we fix our nation’s Air Traffic Control system now."
Kirby said lawmakers from both parties were committed to modernizing the system while holding the FAA accountable.
Fox News' Grady Trimble, Anders Hagstrom, Stephen Sorace, Trey Wallace, and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Harry Kane equals 78-year record from England icon
keyFacts: Harry Kane scored a penalty against Spain to equal Tom Finney's 78-year-old record of scoring in seven consecutive England away matches.
The victory enabled Thomas Tuchel's England to top their Nations League group as Kane extended his overall record to 93 goals.
England will play a two-legged Nations League quarter-final tie during the March international break.
body: Harry Kane has become the first England player for 78 years to score in seven consecutive away matches.
The Three Lions captain opened the scoring from the penalty spot against Spain on Sunday night.
Kane has scored in seven consecutive away matches for England Getty
His 93rd international goal extended his record of scoring in every fixture during the current Nations League campaign.
Meanwhile, Kane has also matched a scoring feat which had been unmatched since 1948.
Dating back to June 2025, he has scored in each of England ‘s last seven away fixtures.
The last trip to a non-neutral venue without Kane on the scoresheet came against Greece in November 2024.
Record-equalling goal
He is the first Three Lions player to do so since legendary Tom Finney, who did so between September 1946 and May 1948.
Kane and Finney are the only two players in history to score in seven successive away appearances for England.
The former will have to wait until March to extend his run to eight, though, with the trip to Spain their last of 2026.
His effort broke the deadlock in the final minute of the first half at the Metropolitano Stadium.
Ezri Konsa added a second for the visitors with a bullet header from a corner just eight minutes after the restart.
The defender’s Arsenal team-mate Ben White made it three for England four minutes later on a dominant night in the Spanish capital.
Kane is the first England player since Finney in 1948 to achieve the feat Getty
A victory will see Thomas Tuchel’s side top their Nations League group at the expense of their opponents.
Both sides had already qualified for the quarter-finals ahead of their final league phase outing.
The four group winners will be drawn against the four runners-up for a two-legged tie during the March international break .
A semi-final berth in June will then await the winners of those contests.
Kane on target
As for Kane, he has now extended his all-time scoring record for England to 93 goals in 127 caps.
The 33-year-old also redeemed his penalty miss against Spain at Wembley Stadium back in September.
Kane has scored in each of England’s six Nations League matches Getty
It was only his fifth penalty miss for the Three Lions and his first since their quarter-final defeat to France at the 2022 World Cup.
He had already scored in their opener against Spain, kickstarting a run of scoring in all six Nations League fixtures.
Those matches have produced eight goals for Kane, who grabbed a brace in wins over both Croatia and the Czech Republic.
The Bayern Munich striker subsequently leads the Nations League scoring charts as he aims to win the golden boot for the first time.

articles.headline: You can control your other devices with this resourceful Apple feature
keyFacts: Apple's iOS Switch Control feature allows users to control other devices on the same Wi-Fi network remotely.
The accessibility tool supports alternate inputs like head movements, adaptive controllers, and standard gamepads for people with limited mobility.
Users can record and replay input sequences called Recipes to automate repetitive actions in mobile games and reading apps.
body: You can control your other devices with this resourceful Apple feature
This accessibility feature can be really useful.

With iOS's Switch Control, you can control your iPhone or iPad using alternate input methods ranging from external adaptive controllers to head movements and hand gestures. It's a useful accessibility feature for anyone with limited mobility that's even more powerful than it might seem at first if you dig into its settings. One option, Use Other Devices for Switch Control, lets you use the alternate controls you set up on one iOS device to control other devices on the same Wi-Fi network, and it only takes a little bit of setup.

First, you need to enable Switch Control across your devices. Make sure any devices you want to control are connected to the same Wi-Fi network and you're signed into the same iCloud account on all of them. If you want to control a Mac desktop computer remotely, you also need to open the Apple menu, click Accessibility and open the Switch Control menu. Select Allow platform switching to control your computer. Then on your mobile devices, open the Settings app, click Accessibility and turn the Switch Control toggle on. Now you can assign external controllers or gestures to specific actions by selecting Add New Switch under the Switches menu and following the onscreen prompts.

Once you have your switches set up, head back to the main Switch Control menu and select Device, then Use Other Device. This will show you a list of all the compatible devices linked to your network. Select one and you can use the switches you've already established to control them remotely. When you want to stop controlling the remote device, just select Stop Using Device under the same menu.
Switch Control is more versatile than it looks

While Switch Control's Use Other Devices feature can only be used to control iOS devices, you can assign non-Apple devices as your external controllers. Adaptive controllers made by other companies like Microsoft can be mapped as switches, but you can even use devices that aren't intended as accessibility tools. Standard game controllers work as well, along with other devices that can connect to your iPhone or iPad via Bluetooth or USB, like Bluetooth keyboards.

Switch Control is intended to make navigating iOS devices and selecting items on screen easier for people with limited mobility, but some users have found novel ways to use it for more than basic functionality. Switch Control lets you set up Recipes, which can be used to record and replay sequences of inputs. With a little work, iOS users have set up Switch Control to automate repetitive actions in mobile games or other apps and to turn pages in the Kindle app. These unintended applications may not always be the best use of Switch Control, but it's worth experimenting with how you can use the feature, especially if you've got multiple iOS devices and want to try controlling them all from one place.

body: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a statement from Megaspeed claiming that Alice Huang hasn’t worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers.
Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama

articles.headline: SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft
keyFacts: Saturday Night Live aired a sketch featuring impressions of tech executives like Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Mark Zuckerberg.
The sketch followed Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Host John Mulaney portrayed a CIA agent explaining to the fictional executives how to avoid being targeted by romantic spies.
body: While awkward, creepy tech executives have become a recurring theme on Saturday Night Live, this week’s episode gave the cast a chance to show off all their impressions at once.

In a single sketch, we got James Austin Johnson as Peter Thiel, Ben Marshall as Sam Altman, Jane Wickline as Dario Amodei, Jeremy Culhane as Elon Musk, Andrew Dismukes as Mark Zuckerberg — and eventually, the recently departed Bowen Yang joined the fun as Jensen Huang.

Huang’s ouster from Nvidia (after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy) could have serious implications for the tech industry; it also provided a hook for some easy jokes about rich nerds being easy marks for women (or men) who are out of their league.

In the sketch, a CIA agent played by host John Mulaney (hilarious as ever, if not entirely confident about how to pronounce “Palantir” or “Nvidia”) attempts to painstakingly explain why these execs should be suspicious when someone attractive suddenly seems interested in them romantically. For Altman and Thiel’s sake, he added, “I hope this is obvious: Even though you’re gay, you can still be tricked by a spy.”

Johnson’s version of Thiel pushed back, insisting that that tech tycoons deserve more respect, given all they’ve done for the country. “Name one time technology has let us down,” he said, giving Mulaney a chance to remind viewers about flights being halted all across the United States on Friday night.

“Okay, name one more time,” the fictional Thiel said, leading to an obligatory mention of Microsoft Outlook going down on Thursday. When asked for a third example, Mulaney said, “No, I’m done naming times.”

“Look, I get it,” he said. “I can’t imagine how disorienting this has been for you, to go from being bug-eyed weirdos to being gods. I mean, never in the history of our species have people as pale and as strange as you a) survived, and b) been given all the world’s wealth and power.”

articles.headline: Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s No. 1 cause of death officially revealed
keyFacts: The Ocarina of Time remake reportedly sold over 5.2 million copies on the Nintendo Switch 2 less than four days after launch.
Global player data from the free Zelda Notes app shows ReDeads are the leading cause of player deaths at 18 percent.
Global player data is subject to change as more people complete playthroughs of the Ocarina of Time remake.
body: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has officially been out for more than two weeks, and saying its reception has been good would be an understatement. It was named the No. 2 best-selling game on the Nintendo Switch 2, with over 5.2 million copies reportedly sold less than four days after launch. Longtime Zelda fans and newcomers alike have been enjoying revisiting the 1998 classic in this remake.

The Ocarina of Time remake comes with a few bonuses thanks to it being brought into the modern gaming scene. Among them are the ability to play songs on the Ocarina through the game's built-in microphone and, perhaps most exciting of all, the option to download a companion app to track your personalized playthrough data. The Zelda Notes app is a free service accessible through the Nintendo Switch app on your phone, and it can provide insight into not only how your playthrough has been going, but also how it compares to players globally. Through the Hall of Fallen Heroes, you can compare how many enemies you've defeated with players worldwide, and see details such as how far you've traveled or how many "game overs" you've had.
Zelda Notes app reveals No. 1 cause of death in Ocarina of Time

Now that the Ocarina of Time remake has been out for a few weeks, global data stored in the Zelda Notes app is revealing certain details about the way people are playing the game, including the No. 1 cause of death for players. ReDeads are the most dangerous enemies, with 18% of players falling victim to the zombie-like monsters that can paralyze Link with fear.
Other global data revealed by the Zelda Notes app includes:
- Skulltullas are the most commonly defeated enemy type.
- ReDeads/Gibdos are the leading cause of "game overs."
- Traps are the leading source of damage, followed closely by ReDeads/Gibdos.
- Dark Link is the miniboss that has caused the most "game overs."
- Deku Seeds are the most commonly used consumable, followed closely by arrows and bombs.
- The Hookshot is the most commonly used special item, followed by the slingshot, boomerang, and bow.
- The Lens of Truth is the most-used magic item, followed by Din's Fire.
- The most common clear time for Ocarina of Time is in the range of 20 to 30 hours.
Keep in mind that global data is subject to change as more people complete playthroughs of the Ocarina of Time remake, but it's interesting to see the early waves of data now available.

articles.headline: White House counsel promises ‘vigorous response’ to Democrats’ oversight threats
keyFacts: White House counsel Will Scharf warned incoming House oversight chairman Robert Garcia that Democratic investigations will face a vigorous response.

body: White House counsel Will Scharf promised to respond in a “vigorous” way to Democrats’ threats of increased oversight against the Trump administration in their new congressional majorities.

Scharf wrote to Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA), the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, last week, warning the California congressman, who told the Trump administration to “lawyer up” on election night , against intimidating members of the administration through investigations. He spoke on Fox News Sunday about the letter and his message to House Democrats.

“Congressman Garcia, other Democrat members of Congress, are intent on threatening and intimidating members of this administration from the president on down to the most junior staffer,” Scharf said. “If that’s the approach that they’re going to take, they’re going to be met with a vigorous response from my office and from the Department of Justice every single time.”
Scharf ridiculed a quote from Garcia, in which the congressman said “pettiness” could be a factor in Democrats holding the Trump administration accountable.
“Maybe it’s because I’m gay, but pettiness is a thing,” Garcia said Saturday . “We’re not going to forget these crimes.”
Scharf criticized Garcia’s rhetoric on Sunday.

“The only shocking thing is some of the terrible statements that Congressman Garcia has been making for weeks now. He said that his desire to investigate this administration was born out of his own pettiness. Pettiness is not a valid purpose to conduct oversight under our Constitution and under our laws,” Scharf said.
WHITE HOUSE WARNS HOUSE DEMOCRATS NOT TO HARASS STAFF WITH OVERSIGHT INVESTIGATIONS

Garcia took the letter this week from Scharf as a “threat,” telling MSNow that President Donald Trump and the White House’s rhetoric around Democratic oversight should be taken seriously, but that it will not change their posture.

“We are going to continue to aggressively investigate these serious allegations of crime between the Trump crime family, corporate America. What’s happening with DHS and ICE. The Jeffrey Epstein investigation. I mean, the list goes on and on. And Donald Trump is clearly hiding something,” Garcia said on the network in response to the letter.

articles.headline: London City's 'bravery' paying off in top three pursuit
keyFacts: London City Lionesses drew 1-1 against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in a Women's Super League match.
London City sits third in the table, holding the final qualification spot for next season's Women's Champions League.
London City holds a six-point lead over Arsenal, with current league leaders Chelsea awaiting them in December.
body: - Published
After 10 games in the Women's Super League season, London City Lionesses have shown they are capable of finishing inside the top three.
Their narrow 2-1 defeat by Manchester City two weeks ago provided snippets of their potential but a 1-1 draw at the Emirates against an improved Arsenal on Sunday confirmed their credentials.
Eder Maestre's side sit third in the table - the last qualification spot for next season's Women's Champions League - and are six points above Arsenal.
It is a strong position to be in just shy of the halfway stage having already faced big hitters Arsenal, Manchester City and Manchester United.
Current leaders Chelsea await in December but, for now, London City's progress is moving at a pace that looks set to challenge the usual suspects.
Showing 'bravery' at the Emirates
A sold-out away end helped fill out the 32,000-strong crowd at the Emirates on Sunday as many hoped for an end-to-end encounter.
They were not disappointed as fearless London City showed bravery against an Arsenal side who played with a spark following their 1-1 draw with Barcelona.
The visitors were helped out by Arsenal's wastefulness - the Gunners had 17 shots and only converted one - but London City caused plenty of problems of their own.
Maestre said after their defeat by Manchester City that their opponents showed more experience and know-how but against Arsenal, his side matured.
They were under pressure early on and fell a goal down thanks to Frida Maanum's opener but it took just 98 seconds for Izzy Goodwin to equalise for London City.
That killed Arsenal's momentum and when the pressure increased again from the hosts in the second half, goalkeeper and player of the match Mary Earps stepped up to make crucial saves.
"The performance was there. We had the chances to score and get a better result but Arsenal had chances too. The game was very open," said Maestre.
"The way we faced and challenged every circumstance in the game shows we are here, and able to play with that mentality in these big games.
"We came here to take risks. Our energy was good. We were brave and weren't scared about the context or the opponent.
"We tried to play as if we were at home. I always want to feel that my teams are brave and go for the win."
That bravery showed as Alexia Putellas came close twice with long-range efforts, Goodwin could have been onside when she was played in behind later on.
London City hit the crossbar through substitute Delphine Cascarino and had 14 shots compared to Arsenal's 17, including four inside the box.
Arsenal are still yet to win at home this season in the WSL but this was still an impressive showing from London City, who came to the Emirates to play.
But while they were willing to take risks, they were smarter than they were against Manchester City, choosing when to press aggressively and when to hold off.
"We tried to match the pace of the ball and not expose ourselves as much to the players that Arsenal have," added Maestre.
"We were trying to mix the moments we were more clinical in our press. We made some adjustments at half-time and were much better at recognising those."
Earps and Goodwin shine on big stage
London City are backed by US billionaire Michele Kang and that has made a big difference in the transfer market.
They recruited superstars Alexia Putellas, Mary Earps, Mapi Leon and Kadidiatou Diani in the summer.
Such is their depth that high-flying Spaniard Lucia Corrales, the dangerous Cascarino and England international Freya Godfrey came off the bench.
Those individual talents have made a difference and on Sunday it was goalkeeper Earps who took the plaudits, claiming the player of the match award.
She made crucial saves late on as Arsenal pushed ferociously for a winner, tipping Maanum's effort onto the crossbar and blocking her shot from close range.
Earps had to bide her time for the number one shirt after making the switch from Paris St-Germain this summer but has started the past three WSL games.
"Mary is a very strong character and is much more than the things we see in terms of the performance," said Maestre.
"She has experience, and energy that you can bring to every part in the process and not just the things we see in the matches.
"I think the energy that she brings to the position is massive and has a massive impact. I'm very pleased with her."
Watching on in the stands was England boss Sarina Wiegman who will have been pleased with the display from goalscorer Goodwin.
The 23-year-old got the better of England captain Leah Williamson when she fooled her with quick feet and fired the ball into the back of the net, making it 1-1.
She is proof that competition for places in the London City starting XI is pushing players on and that their depth is improving each week.
"I think Izzy is becoming a more mature player. She has the inner competition and the signings sometimes push you to bring 100% every time," added Maestre.
"She is committed to keep pushing and, with the performances she is having, why not [earn an England call-up]?
"Izzy is moving forward in the ways she can take advantage and that commitment is the way she is reaching those performances. I'm very proud of her."

articles.headline: All Hail Blood Gulch, Halo’s Greatest Multiplayer Map
keyFacts: Halo's Blood Gulch multiplayer map became popular among players through local split-screen matches and System Link LAN connections.
Blood Gulch was recreated in subsequent Halo entries, other video games like Fortnite, and the web series Red vs. Blue.
A 2018 System Link update for Halo: The Master Chief Collection allowed former players to reunite for LAN matches on Blood Gulch.
body: After 25 years, Halo can be remembered for many things. It's among the best launch games of all time, which was pivotal in making Xbox a serious console contender. Its campaign was so brilliantly designed, from set pieces like The Silent Cartographer to the distinct and believable AI behaviors, that it was one of the few games at the time that compelled me to replay on its hardest difficulty.

But perhaps what has made it so meaningful and memorable over the years--which is sadly absent from the recent Halo: Campaign Evolved--is its competitive multiplayer. And I can't really think about Halo multiplayer without thinking of Blood Gulch, especially when it was essentially the only map I would ever play with friends.

Multiplayer sessions fixated on just one map was a bit of a common occurrence among my friends, given the countless sleepovers that involved GoldenEye on the N64 and doing nothing but having shootouts in the toilets of Facility. In comparison, Halo took a while to make an imprint for us, considering that I had to wait until the following Christmas after its launch before I could get an Xbox.

I was also the only person among my friends to own Microsoft's console, but Halo's influence would spread like The Flood when I introduced it to my friend Josh. We had gone to different schools in sixth form but stayed in touch as I was going to church back then, so it became a ritual that after evening service, he would come around to my place to work through Halo's campaign in co-op. By the end of its explosive final mission, he was converted and got his own Xbox.
Halo: Combat Evolved - Blood Gulch

It was also at this point where we were able to meaningfully experience Halo's multiplayer. After all, shooting at each other in 1v1 matches was a bit one-note, but Josh also had younger brothers, so suddenly I was going over to his house with spare controllers so we could play four-player splits-screen just like the N64 days. This was when we got our introduction to Blood Gulch, a name I had only been able to read about for months, but would become permanently etched from thereon.

On the face of it, Blood Gulch is the antithesis of a typical FPS map, its canyon design giving too much space in a genre that's often more fast-paced, with fewer tactical corners to poke around. However, the open field was also what made it viable for vehicular action, letting you rampage with your pal on a Warthog or run someone over with a Ghost. But when thinking of its semi-symmetrical layout with a base at each end, it also brings to mind a large football field, which also leads me to Capture the Flag.

Halo may not have invented this mode, but as a console gamer first, it was my real introduction to it, and felt transformative. While in the days of GoldenEye we would quite happily run around shooting each other, now we actually had a concrete goal to work towardr as a team, which also didn't feel completely different from the attack and defense of five-a-side football.
Halo: Combat Evolved - Blood Gulch

Even so, there's only so much potential you can wring out of 2v2 CTF, with one side haplessly carrying the flag while the other tries to fight off the opposing Spartans, and we occasionally made things harder on ourselves by turning off vehicles.

The bigger game changer was discovering the System Link Cable that allowed us to connect multiple Xbox consoles together, which was how I got my first taste of a LAN party. I could also count on Josh to evangelize on Halo's behalf so that we ended up roping in enough folks from church to get together for 4v4 matches (this was still only half of its full potential, as it was actually possible to connect up to four Xbox systems for 16-player multiplayer).

It was via this method that we really got to appreciate the balanced yet asymmetrical design of Blood Gulch, such as how the Red team has access to a ridge that's a perfect sniping spot, while the Blue team is closer to a tunnel system, though that doesn't prevent each team from taking advantage of either route. The base would be at one moment a quiet place to shoot banter with another defending teammate before exploding into tight shootouts when someone tried to make a scramble for the flag.

I've played many more team-based FPS games over the years too, but few ever have as as memorable a moments ascatching the glint of a sniper hiding behind Sniper's Rock and then trying to sneak your way up to take them out first, the foolhardy derring-do of stealing a flag while praying your invisibility power-up lasts, or having everyone pile into a Scorpion tank and going in loud.
Halo: Combat Evolved - Blood Gulch

Given the setup required, I would be lying if I said I got to experience Halo via System Link more than a handful of times. After all, the first time we managed to organize this event was the summer before I went away to university, where I was back to being the only person in my immediate circle who was gaming, let alone an Xbox owner. Of course, the year Halo 2 came out and I was back for the holidays, we naturally wrangled people together again to link up and load up its Blood Gulch remake, Coagulation, taking to the new additions like energy swords and Banshees even if they might have upset its predecessor's balance. It's the seemingly all-night-long sessions at Blood Gulch that are so burned into my memory.

I don't think I'm alone in that, given the map's popularity over the years, having not only been remade by Bungie in subsequent entries, but even by the community the moment the Forge update was added to Halo Infinite. In later years, its beloved status has found it being remade in other shooters, including CS:GO and Fortnite. But beyond the genre, its cultdom was arguably cemented by the web series Red vs. Blue, its creator Burnie Burns perfectly tapping into its desolate desert as a space for contemplating existentialist themes on almost the same level as a Samuel Beckett play.

But for all the ways that Halo has evolved over the years, for me it was Halo: The Master Chief Collection getting a System Link update in 2018 that was the most meaningful. Over that time, I had stopped going to church and even spent many years a lapsed gamer, but once the habit had kicked back in, I had also gotten back in touch with Josh. While we had caught up with various online multiplayer games, such as Destiny and Overwatch, the opportunity to relive Halo LAN parties 15 years later was something we just had to seize.
Halo: Combat Evolved - Blood Gulch

Of course, we had all gotten older with more responsibilities and busy schedules, but there was something special about how despite the different paths we'd taken, Halo somehow brought us back together for one night, albeit with each team huddling around a larger and sharper monitor than the CRT TVs we made do with back in the day. And despite Halo MCC including the new Bloodlines map--a remake of Coagulation--when it came to setting up a Capture the Flag session, there was no question that Blood Gulch was our unanimous pick as a pure nostalgia hit.

Halo may feel like a shadow of its former self these days, its recent campaign remake feeling more like a pristine eulogy than a path toward the future, which will now be under the direction of Activision.
But no matter how bleak or uncertain that future looks, at least we'll always have Blood Gulch.

articles.headline: Senator-elect Scott Colom vows to ensure Trump follows through on his promises
keyFacts: Democrat Scott Colom unseated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi's first Black US senator since 1875.
Colom pledged to ensure Donald Trump follows through on campaign commitments regarding consumer prices, foreign wars, and Jeffrey Epstein files.
Trump stated he will wield his veto powers to dictate policy when Democrats take control of Congress in January.
body: After recently becoming the first Mississippi Democrat elected to the US Senate in more than four decades, Scott Colom pledged to try to ensure Donald Trump “follows through on the commitments” he made while successfully running for a second presidency in 2024.

Colom, while being interviewed by CNN host Dana Bash on Sunday, alluded to various campaign promises made by Trump – including lowering consumer prices, halting the seemingly endless wars waged under other presidential administrations, and fully releasing files related to the prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein, the late accused sex trafficker whose social circle encompassed the US and global elite.

But prices for fuel and other goods soared as Trump and Israel started war in Iran in February, a conflict which has dragged on for months – and critics have said many of the so-called Epstein files have been excluded from allegedly incomplete disclosures by the president’s administration.
Voters “elected me to make sure he follows through on the commitments he made in 2024,” Colom said. “Well, I want to work … to actually accomplish that.”

Colom also said that he intended to support efforts to pass legislation restricting stock trading by members of Congress, saying it was important for Americans to know lawmakers at the US Capitol in Washington DC “aren’t making money instead of looking out for them”.
“We [have] got to look out for our families – not DC families,” Colom said.
In a separate interview with NBC News’s Kristen Welker on Sunday, Colom added: “I’m not here to look out for the billionaires. I’m here to look out for working people.”

Those remarks from Colom came after he unseated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith during the 3 November midterm elections to become the first Black US senator from Mississippi since 1875 – during the Reconstruction period after the American civil war.

Colom’s triumph over Hyde-Smith occurred about three years after she blocked the former state prosecutor’s nomination for a federal judgeship during Joe Biden’s presidency, which interrupted Trump’s two White House terms. In many ways Colom’s victory punctuated a midterm “blue wave” that saw Trump and his Republican party lose control of Congress to their Democratic counterparts for the latter half of his second presidency beginning in January.

With the outcome of the US Senate race in Alaska still pending on Sunday, the seat to which Colom was elected was among eight that the Democrats had flipped in that congressional chamber. Democrats had also gained more than three dozen seats in the US House during the midterms while significantly expanding their control of state governors’ offices, igniting hopes among the party’s supporters that it could impede Trump’s agenda for the rest of his time in power.

Trump has responded to the new political reality for the rest of his presidency by reminding the public that he has veto powers which he can wield to dictate policy with respect to matters such as the Iran war.

Asked by Bash to reflect on the historic significance of his win over Hyde-Smith, Colom replied: “It says that we have made a lot of progress in the journey to have people judged by the content of their character and not the color of their skin.
“I had faith that Mississippians would give me a chance … if I could get my values out there and a vision for our state out there,” Colom said. “And – you know – Mississippi proved me right.”

Colom appeared on both networks remotely from Atlanta, where he was stranded after his flight to Washington DC was cancelled in the chaotic aftermath of Friday’s nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop.
From Atlanta’s airport on Saturday night, Colom documented the frustrations of fellow travelers on social media.

The senator-elect said one traveler even made a reference to his viral campaign ad criticizing Hyde-Smith for once suggesting those concerned about rising beef prices could opt for cheaper sources of protein.
The campaign ad’s tagline was: “Pick another protein? … I’d rather pick another senator instead.”

As the clock passed midnight at the airport, Colom wrote that another passenger made a joke at the expense of Trump’s transportation secretary Sean Duffy, saying, “Pick another flight? … pick another transportation secretary.”

articles.headline: Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside the company for new CEO after Jensen Huang’s resignation: ‘Dramatic shakeup’
keyFacts: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, prompting Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to urge the board to choose an outside successor.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia owes the administration answers within ten days regarding whether it profited from banned chip sales.
Jensen Huang agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, while Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday.
body: Nvidia should look “outside the company” to replace its CEO, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said — but it shouldn’t wait too Huang.
Founder Jensen Huang famously had no succession plan and the board must now push a “dramatic shakeup,” Bessent told Larry Kudlow Sunday on Fox News’ “Sunday Morning Futures.”
The $4 trillion firm also owes the Trump administration answers within 10 days about whether it was profiting off of banned chip sales.
“I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said.
“And I think we need answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel.”
Huang, 63, resigned last week as president, CEO and director of the company, which he cofounded at a Denny’s in 1993.
“This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company,” Bessent said. “They needed a dramatic shakeup.”
The Treasury secretary has spent the week pressing a narrower question than who’s sleeping with whom: who bought Nvidia’s chips, and where they ended up.
Alice Huang was an executive for the Singapore-based, Alibaba-backed datacenter company Megaspeed, which has been accused of smuggling high-end Nvidia chips to China — despite a US ban.

“The real story here should be, did Nvidia know their client?” Bessent said Friday on CNBC. He added that anyone at the company responsible for letting chips slip through the cracks should be “held accountable.”
“We do not know for a fact that Jensen Huang knew this,” he added.
He said Treasury, the State Department, the Defense Department and the US Trade Representative had backed blacklisting Megaspeed “for months.”
Nvidia will report quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first report without Huang at the helm.
Huang has also agreed to a closed-door interview with three House committees Dec. 1, and the Senate Banking Committee has asked him to testify the same week.

articles.headline: Are you more of an ambient music enjoyer or theatrical atmosphere appreciator?
keyFacts: The author expressed a newly found appreciation for World of Warcraft's ambient music after initially wanting more theatricality.
The author contrasted ambient game soundtracks like Minecraft and Mirror's Edge with the grand thematic music of Final Fantasy 14.
The author invited readers to leave comments sharing whether they prefer atmospheric or dramatic video game soundtracks.
body: When World of Warcraft: Forever's beta first launched, I lamented its long stretches of silence and penchant for ambience over theatrics. I still sort of stand by that, but after spending more time in Azeroth (and discovering the loop music setting) I've a new-found appreciation for both WoW's soundtrack and ambient music as a whole.

It's also got me thinking about what makes a soundtrack ambient versus something more melodic. I'm chronically Final Fantasy 14-brained, where just about everything has a grand thematic soundtrack to it—the jauntiness of the Gold Saucer, the soothing Middle-earthness of Gridania's outer Shroud zones, the grand organs of Ishgard's bitterly cold landscape. You can't escape composer Masayoshi Soken's penchant for leifmotifs. He will turn anything into an orchestral spectacle.

I'm a big JRPG fan in general, a genre I think is the absolute master of thematic soundtracks. But I also think fondly of games I've played over the years that are a little more pared down, their soundtracks there for a little atmosphere rather than actively driving the narrative. Minecraft's OST is a masterclass in ambience, and is in regular rotation across my videogame-themed Spotify playlists. I also have a huge soft spot for the soundtrack behind Mirror's Edge—one which settles in this almost otherworldly ambiance, only ramping up when Faith is in a perilous situation.

But what about you? Do you prefer the more subtle nuances that an atmospheric soundtrack has to offer? Or do you like your videogame music loud, in your face, and full of dramatics? Be sure to leave a comment and let me know which one's your favourite and why.

body: Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.
According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

"Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."
"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."
